decision: Reject all three tested runtime variants. Allocation-call reductions are accompanied by repeated scalar slowdowns, larger temporary layouts, requested-byte/peak increases and larger probe executables. These data do not support advancing the variants to native admission. Performance ranks above memory and binary size; isolated heap savings do not justify the observed regressions.
qualification: Each variant passes eight new storage controls, six inherited cache-frontier tests, eleven admitted P4 tests, 882 all-feature scalar library tests, 795 default scalar library tests and 28 doctests. Formatting, strict default/all-feature/all-target Clippy and warning-denied scalar docs pass. Counts overlap; these are not unique or full-workflow totals.
limits: Block ratios pair each candidate with the baseline in the same fixed block; this is a four-variant design, not additional samples for any earlier experiment.
Ratios and directions are descriptive, without statistical-significance or application-speedup claims. Every range and adverse row is retained.

Requested Rust allocations exclude native C heaps, stack frames and allocator bookkeeping; retained and peak counters are phase-relative and do not prove eventual reclamation. Increased temporary layouts are reported separately.
Probe binary sizes are not production executable size. Native consumers, full reports, the complete workflow/feature/target matrix and original limits remain open.
All retained requested-byte deltas match in all five pairs and every phase. This does not establish identical stack use or total memory.

This is a decision based on the measured workload and priority ladder, not a universal claim that inline storage is slower. No native timing gate, native control, full-report replay or production CLI build was executed for these rejected variants.

The uninstrumented parent still fails its original board limit at 133.31248412 seconds of worker CPU against 120; the separate original neck assertion passes. These are parent results, not timing results for the rejected storage variants.

next_experiment.question: Can one inline radical slot keep the original coefficient size by using SmallVec union storage, while preserving performance against both the original and a feature-only control?

source_review.observation: Without union, SmallVecData is an enum; with union it overlays inline and heap storage and reuses capacity to distinguish them. This motivates a smaller-layout hypothesis. The current experiment did not enable union. Layout changes alone do not explain or prove the cause of the timing regressions.
